 Egypt and Malawi meet in the third round of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers on Friday, 13 November, with kick-off scheduled for 19:00 (UK time). The match takes place in Cairo, where the hosts will be looking to strengthen their position at the top of Group B.
 The Pharaohs have collected four points from their opening two matches and lead the group on goal difference, while Malawi sit third, just one point behind. Egypt will also be playing their first match under new head coach Ali Maher, who replaced Hossam Hassan earlier this month.
 Read on for our Egypt vs Malawi analysis, sports betting tips, predicted line-ups, and where to watch the match.

 Egypt vs. Malawi - Head-to-head record
 Egypt have enjoyed the better of their previous meetings with Malawi , winning four of their six encounters, drawing one and losing the other. Their two most recent clashes came during qualifying for the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations.
 The Pharaohs won 2-0 at home in March 2023 before recording an even more convincing 4-0 victory in the reverse fixture four days later. Malawi failed to score in either match, conceding six goals across the two encounters.

 Egypt – A New Era Begins Under Ali Maher
 Egypt lead Group B with four points from their opening two qualifiers, but their recent performances have been mixed. With Ali Maher preparing for his first match in charge, let’s examine the Pharaohs’ recent results and expected line-up.
 Recent form
 Egypt began their qualification campaign with a disappointing goalless draw against Angola before responding with a commanding 5-0 victory away to South Sudan. Those results leave them unbeaten in the group and yet to concede a goal.
 However, their wider form has been less convincing. The Pharaohs have managed just two victories in normal time across their last nine matches , while their most recent outing ended in a 1-0 friendly defeat to South Africa in Cairo.
 That defeat proved to be Hossam Hassan’s final match in charge, with the Egyptian Football Association dismissing him on 7 November. His replacement, Ali Maher, has recalled several players, including Mohamed El Shenawy, Mahmoud Hamdy El Wensh, Mohamed Shehata, Mahmoud Marei and Nasser Maher.
 Mohamed Salah returns after missing the previous two matches, while Trezeguet is available again following injury. Omar Marmoush is also expected to start. However, Mostafa Ziko is suspended following a five-match FIFA ban, and Hamdy Fathy is unavailable through injury.

 Malawi - Looking for some consistency
 Malawi have collected three points from their first two qualifiers, but their poor recent away record raises concerns ahead of the trip to Cairo. Let’s take a closer look at their performances and expected line-up.
 Recent form
 Malawi began their Africa Cup of Nations qualification campaign with a promising 2-1 home victory over South Sudan. However, they failed to build on that result, suffering a 3-1 defeat away to Angola in their following match.
 The Flames have struggled for consistency in recent months, winning just twice in their last nine fixtures across all competitions. During that period, they have recorded two draws and five defeats. Their away record is particularly concerning . Malawi have failed to win any of their last five matches on the road, losing three and failing to score in three.
 Head coach Kalisto Pasuwa faces considerable pressure to secure qualification for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, having acknowledged that his future could depend on the team’s progress. Malawi have appeared at the continental tournament only three times, most recently reaching the last 16 in 2021.
 The visitors will be without defender Dennis Chembezi, who is injured, while forward Mayele Malango is unavailable. Goalkeeper William Thole has also been omitted due to a lack of playing time. There is better news with the return of Lanjesi Nkhoma, who missed the previous three international call-ups.

 Predictions for Egypt vs. Malawi - A comfortable home win
 Egypt’s attacking options have been strengthened by the returns of Mohamed Salah and Trezeguet, while Omar Marmoush is also expected to feature. Against a Malawi side that have struggled away from home, backing Egypt to score in both halves is an interesting option.
 The Pharaohs scored five goals against South Sudan in their previous qualifier and have won their last two meetings with Malawi by at least two goals. This makes Egypt to win and over 2.5 goals another appealing market.
 Despite the uncertainty surrounding the managerial change, Egypt have considerably more attacking quality and a strong recent head-to-head record. Our main prediction is Egypt to win with a -1.5 handicap , meaning the hosts must win by at least two goals.
